key_insight: Adding a monolayer graphene contact to AlInN/Si solar cells improves current collection and efficiency without changing the open-circuit voltage much.
engineering_relevance: Graphene can serve as a low-temperature, semitransparent conductive contact that enhances nitride-based solar cell performance while remaining compatible with device integration.
method: Built AlxIn1-xN solar cells on p-type Si(100) with a thin a-Si buffer layer
Tested three Al compositions: x = 0.22, 0.35, and 0.43
Transferred monolayer graphene onto the front surface as a semitransparent contact
evidence_signal: Under illuminated and dark measurements, graphene improved short-circuit current density, fill factor, and power conversion efficiency across all compositions, while open-circuit voltage stayed nearly unchanged.
watch_item: The reported gains depend on the quality and uniformity of the graphene transfer, which could be a practical challenge for scalable manufacturing.
paper_title: Enhancement of nitride-based solar cells using graphene as transparent contact layer
